uses: Used successfully by psychiatrists/psychologists for anxiety and mild-to-moderate depression; lay use to elevate mood and ease stress and tension; traditional appetite suppressant on long arid walks. Not hallucinogenic; no documented severe adverse effects or withdrawal.
note: ★ SA native; signature Wildroots story plant (your Parceval thread)
cautions: Do NOT combine with SSRIs / other antidepressants (serotonergic). Avoid in pregnancy. Intoxicating doses cause euphoria then sedation.

uses: Native SA tonic: well-being, immune support, longevity, stress/depression/anxiety; wasting from cancer, TB, AIDS; flu, CFS/ME, viral hepatitis, asthma, bronchitis, type-2 diabetes, mild hypertension, rheumatoid arthritis, peptic ulcer/reflux, menopause. Zulu warriors used it to unwind; widows as an anti-depressant.
note: ★ SA native standout — strong Wildroots fit
cautions: Avoid in pregnancy & breastfeeding; caution with immunosuppressants and in active autoimmune disease.
alsoKnown: Cancer bush; insiswa ('that which takes away the dark')

uses: Valued in Cape herbal practice for urinary and digestive support; reputed for its aromatic volatile oils and diuretic properties; long history in SA indigenous wellness.
note: ★ SA fynbos native — flagship local-apothecary plant
cautions: Avoid in pregnancy & kidney inflammation; can irritate in large doses.
references: General herb sources: Wikipedia; Mount Sinai/UMM herb DB; EMA HMPC monographs; ageless.co.za

uses: South African endemic taken as a caffeine-free infusion; valued for general wellness and as a soothing beverage, with a notable antioxidant profile.
growable: With care — needs acid sandy fynbos soil
cautions: Very safe, caffeine-free; rare interaction with some liver-metabolised meds.
references: General herb sources: Wikipedia; Mount Sinai/UMM herb DB; EMA HMPC monographs; ageless.co.za

uses: Cape native brewed as a sweet herbal tea; valued in SA folk practice for respiratory comfort and general vitality.
cautions: Very safe, caffeine-free; mild phyto-estrogen — caution in hormone-sensitive cases.
references: General herb sources: Wikipedia; Mount Sinai/UMM herb DB; EMA HMPC monographs; ageless.co.za

uses: South African succulent used in Xhosa and Zulu herbalism for skin and wound care; the cooling fresh gel applied topically.
cautions: External/fresh-gel use; do not eat the raw leaf in quantity.
alsoKnown: jelly leaf, burn jelly plant, snake flower
references: General herb sources: Wikipedia; Mount Sinai/UMM herb DB; EMA HMPC monographs; ageless.co.za

uses: Southern African native traditionally smoked or brewed; valued for relaxation and mild euphoric effect; part of regional indigenous botanical knowledge.
cautions: Sedating in quantity; avoid in pregnancy; not the same as cannabis but use sensibly.
references: General herb sources: Wikipedia; Mount Sinai/UMM herb DB; EMA HMPC monographs; ageless.co.za

uses: SA expectorant for dry cough; colds, chest infections, sinusitis, malaria, stomach ulcers, toothache, skin; bark/leaf smoked or as snuff to clear sinuses.
growable: With care — SA native tree, ENDANGERED
note: ★ SA native (use leaf, conserve; do not strip bark)
cautions: ENDANGERED — use cultivated leaf only, never wild bark. Avoid in pregnancy.

uses: Southern African plant used in indigenous herbalism for colds, coughs and warming digestive support; culinary and remedial; limited modern documentation.
note: ★ SA native — grow to conserve, never wild-harvest
cautions: Generally safe; large doses thin blood / caution with anticoagulants & gallstones.
references: General herb sources: Wikipedia; Mount Sinai/UMM herb DB; EMA HMPC monographs; ageless.co.za

uses: Tonic, astringent, diaphoretic, stimulant; internally for depression, apathy, nervous exhaustion, headaches, poor circulation, anxiety-driven digestion; relaxes smooth muscle (digestion, menstrual cramps); topical for rheumatism, hair, skin, circulation; antioxidant/anti-ageing.
cautions: Generally safe in culinary/therapeutic doses; caution if prone to epileptic seizures or allergy; large amounts can irritate the gut.

uses: Wound healing, circulation, memory & concentration, general/adaptogenic tonic, skin (psoriasis, eczema, scars), connective tissue, blood purifier, mild diuretic, anti-stress/anti-anxiety, calming. 3,000 yrs Ayurvedic use; China's 'Fountain of Youth'.
cautions: Avoid in pregnancy & liver disease. May cause drowsiness; large doses can irritate.

uses: Coughs & chest troubles (essential oils); antibacterial vs Streptococci, Staphylococci, Bacillus cereus; rich in phytochemicals, vitamins, minerals, amino acids; rapidly eases cough, fever, sore throat, fatigue, weakness.
note: ★ SA native standout — strong Wildroots fit
cautions: Rare liver reactions reported; avoid with anticoagulants & in pregnancy.

uses: Digestive bitter, antiparasitic; A. afra (native) for colds, fever, coughs, flu.
note: ★ Native A. afra is easy & traditional
cautions: Contains thujone — short-term only; AVOID in pregnancy & epilepsy. Not for long use.
alsoKnown: Wilde-als; absinthe wormwood (SA als = Artemisia afra)
references: General herb sources: Wikipedia; Mount Sinai/UMM herb DB; EMA HMPC monographs; ageless.co.za
